paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, comparing six model configurations across nine language families, with error bars indicating standard deviation. The horizontal axis lists the language families in the order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, while the vertical axis is labeled "effect" and ranges from 0 to 30 with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 5. For each language family, six bars are grouped together, representing the model configurations mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (pink), and XLM-B2 (red). The bars vary in height, with the IE-Indic family showing the tallest bars overall, reaching approximately 25 for XLM-B2, and the Isolate and Uralic families showing the shortest bars, near zero across all models. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, while the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 12. The bars are not sorted in a specific order within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized. The chart provides a detailed comparison of the effects across different language families and model configurations.
